chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad ibn Isa from Muawiya ibn Wahb from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who leads the people in prayer while you are not pleased with him, in a prayer where the recitation is recited aloud. He said: 'When you hear the Book of Allah being recited, be silent to it.'
I said: 'But he testifies against me with shirk (polytheism/disbelief).' He said: 'If he disobeys Allah, then obey Allah.'
I pressed him, but he refused to permit me (to do otherwise). He said: I said to him, 'Should I then pray in my house and then go out to join him?' He said: 'You and that (will suffice/do).'

He said: 'Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) was in the morning prayer, and Ibn al-Kawwa' was reciting behind him: "And certainly We have revealed to you and to those before you, if you should associate [others] with Allah, your work would surely become invalid, and you would surely be among the losers." Ali (peace be upon him) was silent, out of reverence for the Quran, until he finished the verse. Then he returned to his recitation. Then Ibn al-Kawwa' repeated the verse, so Ali (peace be upon him) was silent again. Then he recited, and Ibn al-Kawwa' repeated, and Ali (peace be upon him) was silent.'
"So be patient, indeed the promise of Allah is truth, and let not those who have no certainty deceive you."
Then he completed the surah, then he bowed.

Do you not see that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), while being in prayer, was silent to the recitation of the Quran, then returned to his recitation for himself, and completed the prayer with it? Thus is what the preceding report contained. And it is also possible that the meaning refers to the state of taqiya (dissimulation), because whenever the matter is as we mentioned, it was permissible for him to be silent and recite between himself and his own self. And that which reveals what we mentioned is what he narrated:

key_terms.إِنْ عَصَى اَللَّهَ فَأَطِعِ اَللَّهَ: If he disobeys Allah, then obey Allah
key_terms.تَعْظِيماً لِلْقُرْآنِ: out of reverence for the Quran

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they are not pleased with the Imam's recitation or creed during a loud prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *itma' al-ma'mum* (the follower's silence) during the Imam's recitation, emphasizing that reverence for the Quranic text takes precedence over the follower's personal recitation or internal dissent. It highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) exemplary conduct behind Ibn al-Kawwa', who was known for his distinct creed, demonstrating that the validity of the prayer relies on the Imam's recitation while the follower listens in awe. The text further suggests this ruling may be rooted in *taqiya* (dissimulation), allowing followers to maintain communal unity and prayer validity even when the Imam's theological standing is questionable.
